title: Container Bookings: cancelling a confirmed booking and the cancellation fee
content:
## Policy clause
A Container Bookings booking whose status is confirmed, equipment released or gated in is cancelled on the verified customer's instruction. A booking still in requested status is withdrawn through the confirmation process instead and is never charged a cancellation fee.

Cancelling a booking after its empties were released is done on the same instruction, and cancelling a gated-in booking withdraws the laden containers from the terminal before loading.

The cancellation fee is charged per container on the booking's container count, at the band given by the whole calendar days from the cancellation date to the ETD:
| Days before ETD | Per-container fee taken |
|---|---|
| 14 or more | the tier's fee for 14 or more days |
| 7 to 13 | the tier's fee for 7 to 13 days |
| 3 to 6 | the tier's fee for 3 to 6 days |
| 0 to 2 | the tier's fee for 0 to 2 days |

Days before ETD are the calendar-date difference between the ETD and the cancellation date, ignoring the time of day; a cancellation after the ETD has passed takes the 0 to 2 day band. The total fee on one booking never exceeds the tier's cancellation fee cap per booking, and when the computed fee is 0.00 no fee entry is written.

No cancellation fee is charged when the carrier rolls recorded on the booking over its life have reached the tier's number of carrier rolls for free cancellation, or when the tier's relief for dangerous-goods rejection applies and the line has rejected the dangerous-goods acceptance for this booking. These exemptions do not stack into a credit; they only suppress the fee.

A cancellation fee may be booked only on a booking whose status in the line's system is cancelled. A booking carries at most one cancellation fee.

## Calculation order
1. Count the calendar days from the cancellation date to the ETD (a date after the ETD counts in the 0 to 2 band).
2. Take the per-container fee of that band for the booking's tier.
3. Multiply it by the booking's container count.
4. Take the lower of that product and the tier's cap per booking; the cap applies to the product, not to each container.

## Worked example (hypothetical rates)
*Hypothetical tier, for illustration only:* 3 to 6 day fee of 180.00 per container, cap of 1000.00. A booking of 8 containers with ETD 20 October is cancelled on 15 October: 5 days, so the 3 to 6 band applies; 180.00 multiplied by 8 is 1440.00, which exceeds the cap, so 1000.00 is charged.

## Band boundary cases (hypothetical dates)
- ETD 20 October, cancelled 6 October: 14 days, 14 or more band.
- ETD 20 October, cancelled 7 October: 13 days, 7 to 13 band.
- ETD 20 October, cancelled at 23:50 on 13 October: the time is ignored, 7 days, 7 to 13 band.
- ETD 20 October, cancelled 21 October: after the ETD, 0 to 2 band.

## Exemption truth table
| Carrier rolls have reached the free-cancellation number | Dangerous-goods relief applies and acceptance rejected | Result |
|---|---|---|
| yes | no | no cancellation fee |
| no | yes | no cancellation fee |
| yes | yes | no cancellation fee, and no credit arises |
| no | no | band fee, subject to the cap; no entry when it is 0.00 |
